c74object.name: el.squash~
c74object.description:
el.squash~ is an aggressive dynamic range compressor and expander based on an algorithm by Christopher Penrose. It performs windowed block-level RMS analysis in the time domain using an overlap-add framework to apply radical, colorfully intense compression. Compression is controlled by an inverted ratio parameter where values lower than 1.0 yield heavier compression, 1.0 produces linear response, and values greater than 1.0 expand dynamic range. A dedicated noise threshold (nt) and noise multiplier (nmult) prevent runaway gain on background noise and quiet passages.
Inlets
Inlet 1 [Left Inlet] (signal / messages): Audio input to be compressed, and control message inlet (thresh, ratio, nt, nmult, mute).
Outlets
Outlet 1 (signal): Compressed audio output signal.

inlet.description: Audio input signal to be compressed, as well as parameter configuration messages (thresh, ratio, nt, nmult, mute).

outlet.description: The dynamically compressed audio output signal.

method.name: mute
method.description: When set to 1, mutes DSP computation and outputs silence. When set to 0 (default), normal compression resumes.

method.name: nmult
method.description: Fixed gain multiplier applied when the input RMS level falls below the noise threshold nt and ratio is less than 1.0 (default: 0.1).

method.name: nt
method.description: The baseline noise threshold. Signals with RMS amplitude below this value are scaled by nmult rather than amplified (default: 0.0000001).

method.name: ratio
method.description: Controls dynamic range scaling. Values less than 1.0 compress the dynamic range (smaller values produce more extreme compression); 1.0 represents linear response (no compression, default); values greater than 1.0 produce dynamic expansion.

method.name: thresh
method.description: Linear amplitude threshold above which compression begins to take effect (default: 0.1).

method.name: signal
method.description: Continuous audio stream to be analyzed and dynamically compressed.
